key_insight: Gaussian spatial weighting in PINNs focuses training on shock-like high-gradient regions, enabling better capture of moving and stationary discontinuities without knowing their location in advance.
engineering_relevance: This improves surrogate modeling for low-viscosity fluid flows where sharp fronts are difficult for standard PINNs, making the approach more useful for PDE-constrained engineering prediction and monitoring.
method: Assign Gaussian weights to collocation points based on the PDE residual landscape.
Dynamically emphasize high-gradient/shock regions during optimization.
Apply to 1D quasi-inviscid Burgers’ equations with stationary and moving shocks.
evidence_signal: In the low-viscosity case (ν = 0.0005), the method reduced relative L2 error to about 13% and 14% for stationary and moving shocks, versus 45% and 33% for standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the Gaussian weighting is tuned and may be less straightforward to extend to more complex multidimensional shock structures.
paper_title: G-PINNs: Gaussian-based spatially weighted formulation for PINNs: 1D low-viscous Burgers
